caption:
Foundation Future Industries, a San Francisco startup building humanoid robots for war, missed its October 30 payroll, CNBC reported.
Its CEO Sankaet Pathak had borrowed $4.6 million from the company, and he is its only board member.
Eric Trump is an investor and adviser, and the company is still trying to raise money at a $3 billion valuation.

paragraphs.text: Foundation Future Industries, a San Francisco startup that develops humanoid robots for military and industrial use, missed its October 30, 2026 payroll, according to a CNBC report published on November 14 and summarized by RobotToday and The American Bazaar. People with direct knowledge of the matter said employees had still not received their paychecks.

The American Bazaar reported that this was not the first delay. In August, salaries arrived about two days late after an existing investor provided a bridge loan. Chief executive Sankaet Pathak sent employees a memo saying he was working to secure funds to pay outstanding wages.

According to the reports, Pathak borrowed $4.6 million from the company. Public records show that an LLC listing him as sole principal bought a $4.6 million property in Sausalito, California, in October 2025. Pathak reportedly described the money as a short-term loan, and sources said it did not require separate board approval.

Pathak is the company's sole board member and holds a majority of its shares, a structure that RobotToday said has raised governance concerns among prospective investors. Foundation has been trying to raise hundreds of millions of dollars at a proposed $3 billion valuation since at least January.

Pathak previously cofounded the fintech company Synapse, which collapsed in 2024. Foundation was founded in April 2024 by Pathak, Tribe Capital chief executive Arjun Sethi and Mike LeBlanc, a cofounder of Cobalt Robotics.
Eric Trump and the contract claims

Eric Trump was introduced in April as an investor and chief strategy adviser. The size of his investment has not been disclosed. A spokesperson said he has no role in the company's management, operations, strategy or government contracting.

Foundation has been widely reported to hold about $24 million in Pentagon contracts. CNBC clarified that those research contracts came through Boardwalk Robotics, a Florida company Foundation acquired in late 2024 and the origin of its first robot, the Phantom MK-1, rather than contracts Foundation won directly.

A separate report by the SF Standard, as summarized by AI Weekly, said General Motors described a $300 million order that Foundation cited in 2024 fundraising materials as fabricated. The same report said federal records show no contracts awarded to Foundation itself, and that a journalist who traveled with the team disputed the company's claim that two robots were sent to Ukraine for testing.

In NeuraFeed's reading, the episode shows how far humanoid robot valuations can run ahead of verified revenue. A company asking investors for a $3 billion valuation is now facing questions on basic items such as paying staff, board oversight and whether its largest claimed customers and contracts exist in the form described.
Watch whether Foundation closes new funding and pays its staff, and whether investors or federal agencies respond to the disputed contract and order claims.
